title: Add repository and worktree identities
body:
> [Prototype overview and documentation](https://cli.github.io/multi-account-docs/)
>
> **DO NOT MERGE.** This stack is almost entirely vibe coded. These drafts are for handy review and prototyping, not merging as-is.
>
> Expect the code to be really bad in places: highly coupled, handling edge cases that do not really matter, or doing suspiciously fragile things like parsing GraphQL request bodies.
>
> I suspect some of the suspicious code also exposes the complexity of this feature set, because account selection, Git configuration, scope precedence, worktrees, SSH and API requests all interact.
>
> The prototype experience is the purpose, not the code. I want to find out whether the experience is useful, not defend this implementation or treat it as a design to preserve.

### Description

<!--

Follow on from https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14920

A one-command override still leaves account selection to repeat whenever a developer returns to a repository. This PR adds reusable identities and a repository binding shared by the main checkout and its linked worktrees.

Layer 2 of an eight-part prototype review stack. This is a way to review the design and implementation in smaller pieces, not a proposal to merge the current stack as-is.

I created identities using both real accounts, inspected the generated Git files, and exercised repository-family selection, editing and cleanup. I verified the SSH aliases independently, cloned a private repository, and pushed with ordinary Git.

```text
$ cat ~/.config/gh/identities/personal.gitconfig
# Managed by gh auth identity. Manual changes may be overwritten.
[gh-identity "github.com"]
	name = "personal"
	account = "williammartin"
	sshHost = "github-personal"
[credential "https://github.com"]
	username = "williammartin"
```

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

The identity file contains account metadata and Git preferences, not a credential. The global include loads `auth.gitconfig`, whose `gitdir` conditions select the identity for the common Git directory and linked worktrees.

An SSH alias is a declared connection route, not verified account ownership. The SSH recording checks the account separately with `ssh -T`. Unset, deletion and experiment reset retain saved accounts and credentials.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

This is the foundation layer. Directory and owner bindings, Git attribution, existing SSH-command compatibility and richer explanations are deliberately separate.

I am not sure an identity should support changing its account with `gh auth identity edit --account`. The account feels like part of the identity definition rather than an editable preference. The current implementation allows it, but that is an unresolved design question.

The recordings use the product code at this layer, not a later stack endpoint. The included offline replay scripts are supplementary and do not reproduce the live-account recordings.

<details><summary>Offline replay on macOS</summary>

Build this layer, then run its synthetic scenario with an absolute executable path. This is a replay instruction, not a claim that the command below was used to make the videos.

```sh
make
env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin \
  /bin/bash script/multiaccount-review/02-repository.sh --gh "$PWD/bin/gh"
```

</details>

### Acceptance Criteria

Prototype behaviour under review:

**Given** a reusable identity references a saved account.

**When** I select it with `gh auth use` inside a repository.

**Then** the repository family uses that identity for API requests and independently invoked Git.
